title: `name`
description: The identifier a downstream consumer uses to invoke the tool.
question: Is the tool name unchanged at each capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
known_issues: A prefixed name changes between server configurations, so a hard coded allowlist can silently stop matching.
why: Name based routing, allowlists, and eval fixtures that match exact tool names break under prefixing.

notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: captured tool actions are namespaced as `<serverKey>_<toolName>`, so `delete_account` becomes `src_delete_account`.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the OpenAI request names each function `<plugin>-<tool>` (here `mcp-search_records`), the kernel's fully qualified name. The MCP name survives after the prefix.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` names every tool `<server>_<tool>` (one underscore since 2.0.1, two before), so the model sees `src_search_records` for the server's `search_records`. The prefix is the server key in `servers` and is on by default; the per-server `prefixToolNameWithServerName: false` option, which was not measured, removes it.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): tools reach the model as `<server>-<tool>`, here `src-search_records`. The prefix is the key the host gives the server in `SessionConfig.mcpServers`.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPToolResolver` names a stdio tool `<command>_<args joined by _>_<tool>` and an HTTP or SSE tool `<host>_<port>_<path>_<tool>`, passed through `sanitize_tool_name`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` have no name or prefix option. Measured with the relative launch `python fixtures/tricky_server.py`, `search_records` becomes `python_fixtures_tricky_server_py_search_records`. When the prefix pushes a name past 64 characters it is truncated and an 8-character hash appended, so an absolute launch path can hide the MCP tool name entirely.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: names pass through unchanged, but `deliver_payload` never reaches the model. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` catches any `Throwable` from `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` and only logs it, so a tool it cannot parse is left out of the `ToolRegistry`. Its `mode` property is a `oneOf` of `const`s with no `type`, and the parser throws `IllegalArgumentException: Parameter Delivery mode. must have type property.` (the message uses the property's description where its name belongs). Only a log line records the loss.

verdict.detail: Prefixing is a transformation rather than a loss, but it changes the exact invocation identifier.
